correctness.rationale: From the original coproduct definition, C is coprime iff I⊉C implies C Ann(I)=C for every ideal I. Choose maximal localization C_m nonzero; Nakayama forces C⊆m^n for every nonzero local m^n. Krull intersection then forces nilpotence of mR_m and isolates an Artinian local idempotent summand, while join primality keeps C in that factor. In an Artinian local factor, the condition is C⊆every nonzero ideal; this happens exactly when its socle is one-dimensional, with unique C=socle. Orthogonal factors yield arbitrary closed subsets and hence finite discrete topology. Independent exhaustive tests of ideals, annihilators and original coproduct implication on four F2 algebras confirm 1,1,1,0 coprimes as socle dims 1,1,1,2. The Noetherian generality comes from proof, not four finite rings.
residual_risks: Finite tests alone are not a universal proof.
